transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-05
Time: 10:00 AM PST
Duration: ~72 minutes
Attendees (presented on call): Eleanor Park (CEO), Marco Ruiz (CTO), Priya Shah (VP Product), Hassan Ali (Head of Eng), Lena Ortiz (Head of People), Jonas Meyer (Head of Sales), plus ~40 org attendees (reps from Eng/Product/People/Sales).

Auto-summary (auto-gen may be messy): Q4 focus on tightening latency SLOs while controlling per-token cost; hiring runway and comp band adjustments; SOC2 readiness items mostly on track; follow-ups around benchmarks and hiring documentation.

Topics (auto): Platform perf, routing strategy (dedicated/hosted/private), hiring/people health, security/compliance, Q&A.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Eleanor: Hey everyone, hi thanks for joining — we wanted to do a kind of 90-ish minute, sorry 70, all hands focused on platform priorities and then a people update, so we can keep it tight. If you have questions drop them in the chat, we'll try to take them at the end.

[00:22] Marco: Quick context, I'll do the platform snapshot, Hassan will go into the numbers and tradeoffs, Priya will talk roadmap prioritization, then Lena on hiring, and we'll close with Q&A.

[00:34] Marco: So headline — we've made progress on tail latency and autoscaling, but unit cost per 1k tokens is still above our Q4 target. The main lever is better batching and smarter routing. We're seeing 8-12% improvement with recent kernel tweaks in the hosted path. Caveat: those gains shrink on long sequence lengths.

[00:58] Hassan: Right, uh, the microbenchmarks — quick note, the latest bench spreadsheet (link posted in #all-hands) has percentile breakdowns; P50 looks great, P95 and P99 still have room. We suspect KV cache warm-up patterns -- sometimes the transcriber shows K V cash which is, uh, K-V cache warming is the issue.

[01:18] Audience (Sana): can you define "unit cost" again — are we including infra + egress or just per-token GPU time?

[01:25] Hassan: Good question. For this readout we're reporting infra-excluding-egress: GPU time, instance amortization, and license costs. We'll add a column for net customer cost (incl egress) next week.

[01:40] Marco: On routing: recall we have three main tiers — Hosted API (fastest onboarding), Dedicated (reserved pools) and Private (VPC/on-prem). The strategy is not to push everyone to dedicated; it's a policy-based routing decision. We want predictable SLOs for enterprise customers and low cost for PLG flows.

[02:05] Jonas: From sales feedback, the ask is clearer pricing for Dedicated + guarantees. They're getting pushback in renewals when we can't show predictable paving — um, predictable latency.

[02:20] Priya: Roadmap prioritization: we're proposing three bets for Q1 planning — 1) autoscaling stability + canary policies, 2) cache warming heuristics and prefetch for common prompts, 3) cost-aware compiler optimizations for quantized variants. We'll rank them against OKRs by next Monday.

[02:42] Marco: The compiler work will need sign-off for risky kernel changes; ops will need a rollback path. We also need to validate model accuracy after quant changes. There's a small chance of small distributional shifts, so tie to the Eval team.

[03:05] Eleanor: On the people side, we hit hiring velocity issues. Lena?

[03:12] Lena: Thanks. We had a heavier than usual ramp-off in October, attrition concentrated in infra and one senior product role. We adjusted recruiter funnels and are prioritizing the open SRE and serving-engineer roles. Also, comp bands — HR will circulate a memo with suggested adjustments to keep offers competitive.

[03:34] Audience (Tom): What's the timeline for comp band changes? People are worried about offers on the table turning stale.

[03:39] Lena: We're aiming to finalize by 2025-11-14 and freeze guidance for hiring managers for two weeks after. If you have live offers escalate to me and we'll triage.

[03:55] Hassan: Back to platform — a few specific numbers: average token/sec improved 10% with batching patch; CPU overhead for kernel selection is ~3% but that leads to a 7% median latency improvement. P99 still spikes on cold KV cache and sequencing corner cases when we hit long-chat sessions.

[04:20] Audience (Ava): Are we comfortable with our SOC2 and security posture given more Private deployments?

[04:27] Priya: Compliance update — SOC2 in progress: control remediations nearly done for logging and incident response. SAML/SSO flows were tested last week; KMS integration for Private (customer-managed keys) is in alpha but working for a small pilot.

[04:50] Marco: Note that for Private deployments we have extra networking considerations — customers want fixed VPC endpoints and audit logs; latency there depends on customer's cross-connect. We need a doc for runbooks.

[05:08] Audience (Diego): On the dedicated side, what's the autoscaling policy? How aggressive should we be to avoid cold starts?

[05:16] Hassan: Current default is scale-conservative to meet latency SLAs; we can tune burst windows. There's a tradeoff: more reserved capacity increases cost but lowers tail latency. We'll run a canary next week with a shorter cooldown for a subset of capacity.

[05:42] Priya: For product priorities, we'll use a matrix: impact (customer SLOs, revenue risk) vs complexity (infra changes, eval risk). We're asking teams to submit estimates by Friday.

[06:05] Eleanor: Quick org note — a reminder that comp cycle and performance calibration is upcoming; managers should prepare calibration notes. Also, we're trying a shorter EoQ all-hands format with focused topics instead of doing everything.

[06:22] Audience (Ritika): Any update on the Redwood Optimize feature set and cost-savings suggestions?

[06:28] Marco: Redwood Optimize — the recommendation engine is improving; the next release will give model + quantization suggestions tied to real workload traces. It's still experimental but we have pilot customers saving 10-15% on unit spend.

[06:45] Jonas: Sales wants a playbook for positioning Optimize vs basic tuning — can Product/Sales own a joint doc?

[06:52] Priya: Yes, we'll draft a playbook and put it in the Sales enablement folder; co-authored by Product + Solutions.

[07:05] Audience (Sana): Will the eval checks be automatic so that quantization doesn't regress quality?

[07:12] Marco: We'll gate quantization changes with automated evals on key prompt sets; if regression detected, rollback or fallback to a full-precision variant. This is part of the rollback/rollout policy.

[07:28] Eleanor: Okay let's open it up for live Q&A — please unmute carefully.

[07:35] Audience (unlabeled): [muffled] quick question — is there a plan for region expansion next year? APAC?

[07:42] Eleanor: Yes, APAC is on the roadmap; we're negotiating with two cloud partners and expect a limited region by mid-2026 pending legal/regulatory checks. We'll share more in a regional expansion doc.

[08:00] Audience (Tom): For renewals, customers ask about dedicated SLAs — can we produce standard SLA language?

[08:08] Jonas: We're working on a standardized SLA clause that includes uptime, latency windows for dedicated pools, and remedies. Legal is helping draft.

[08:25] Priya: Quick reminder: link to the benchmark spreadsheet and the roadmap doc placeholder is in the #all-hands channel; please comment with asks.

[08:40] Lena: People matters — tips for managers: be proactive about retention interviews; career ladders are being polished and will be published next week. Also, we plan an AMA with People ops the week after next.

[09:00] Audience (Diego): Two real quick asks: can infra get more headcount for the weekend on-call rotation? And second, can we have a clearer ownership matrix for KV cache priming?

[09:12] Hassan: We'll propose a headcount plan and an interim on-call rotation. Ownership for KV priming — that's infra + serving runtime; I'll write a short RACI and post.

[09:30] Eleanor: Alright, final recap — action items in the chat, next steps are the benchmark + roadmap + comp memos. We'll reconvene for a narrower technical deep-dive next week. Thanks all.

[09:50] Marco: Thanks everyone — feel free to ping us in the leadership channels or DM for sensitive issues.

[10:00] Meeting ends (roughly 72 minutes).

Notes on transcription quality: some names and acronyms were auto-transcribed (e.g., "K-V cash" vs "KV cache", "Red wood" vs "Redwood"). There are occasional overlaps and filler words left in.

Referenced artifacts (links/notes): bench spreadsheet (link posted in #all-hands), roadmap placeholder doc (internal link), comp band memo (draft will be posted by Lena), SOC2 remediation tracker (security channel).

Recap / explicit next steps (verbatim from chat): Hassan to share Q4 latency/cost dashboard by 2025-11-12; Priya will publish roadmap v1 by 2025-11-10; Lena to circulate hiring + comp guidance by 2025-11-14; Marco to schedule engineering deep-dive the week of 2025-11-17.

End of transcript.
